name: Univar Solutions Inc.
warningSignals: Leverage ratio (Net Debt / EBITDA) elevated at 2.8x; refinancing risk if rates remain elevated through 2025
Specialty chemicals segment margin compression YoY; competitive pricing pressure from Asian producers
Working capital intensity rising; inventory turns declining in Q3 vs Q2 — potential demand softening signal
Customer concentration: top 10 customers represent ~35% of revenue; loss of single large account would trigger covenant review
opportunitySignals: ESG-driven demand for sustainable chemistry solutions; Univar's specialty portfolio (bio-based surfactants, low-VOC solvents) gaining traction in CPG supply chains
Consolidation in chemical distribution; Univar positioned as roll-up platform — M&A pipeline active in regional distributors
Margin expansion via digital B2B platform (Nexus); recurring SaaS revenue stream growing 18% YoY, improving cash conversion
Emerging markets (India, Southeast Asia) chemical consumption CAGR 6–8%; Univar expanding regional hubs to capture growth

enginesRun: Nexus digital platform (B2B e-commerce + supply-chain visibility)
Specialty chemicals segment (performance additives, crop protection)
engineOutputs: Digital revenue contribution: ~$180M annualized (2024 run-rate), 12% of total
Specialty chemicals gross margin: 28–30% vs distribution baseline 18–20%
ESG-certified product SKU count: 340+ (2024), up 45% YoY

domainRelevance: Univar Solutions is the largest specialty chemical and ingredient distributor in North America, serving CPG, industrial, agriculture, and water-treatment end-markets. The company's 1,400+ supplier relationships and 8,000+ SKU portfolio position it as a critical node in the supply chain for sustainable chemistry adoption, environmental remediation products, and regulatory-compliant formulations. Univar's digital platform and regional distribution footprint enable rapid deployment of low-carbon and bio-based chemical alternatives to traditional petrochemical-derived inputs.
portalRelevance: Univar is a tier-1 supply-chain orchestrator in the specialty chemicals ecosystem, with direct exposure to environmental regulations (EPA, state VOC limits, REACH compliance) and ESG-driven customer demand. Its financial health and working-capital efficiency are leading indicators of manufacturing activity and consumer-goods production cycles. The company's margin trajectory and customer concentration metrics signal broader shifts in chemical pricing power and consolidation dynamics across industrial supply chains.

notes.cohortStatus: Specialty chemical distributor; peer group includes Wesco International (electrical), ScanSource (IT), Tech Data (IT) — but Univar's chemical-specific exposure and environmental regulatory surface are distinct
notes.envelopeStatus: ELIGIBLE_NOW — public filer, 12+ quarters history, validated financials, active capital markets access

intelligenceCycle.name: Signal Capture
items: Weekly order-intake data by segment (specialty vs distribution) via internal sales dashboards; disclosed in quarterly earnings calls
Supplier price-change notices and commodity hedging activity; reflected in gross-margin variance analysis in 10-K Item 7
Customer inventory levels and demand signals from top-10 accounts; inferred from days-sales-outstanding trends and accounts-receivable aging
Regulatory filings (EPA chemical inventory updates, state VOC compliance certifications); disclosed in 10-K Item 1A risk factors

intelligenceCycle.name: State Estimation
items: Phase classification: P4 (mature, margin-compression cycle); working-capital intensity rising, leverage elevated
Liquidity state: $285M cash, $2.1B debt, 8-quarter runway at current burn; refinancing window opens Q2 2025
Segment health: specialty chemicals growing 8–10% YoY (margin 28–30%), distribution flat to down 2% (margin 18–20%)
Customer concentration risk: top-10 accounts 35% of revenue; single-customer loss would trigger $50–80M revenue impact

intelligenceCycle.name: Diagnosis
items: Pattern match: Univar's margin compression and leverage profile resemble pre-2020 distribution-sector stress; cyclical downturn risk if manufacturing PMI falls below 48
Structural shift: ESG-driven demand for specialty chemistry is real but margin-accretive only if Univar can defend pricing vs. Asian competitors; pricing power test in Q4 2024 earnings
M&A integration risk: Univar has acquired 12+ regional distributors since 2017; synergy realization delays could trigger covenant pressure if EBITDA misses by >5%
Digital inflection: Nexus platform adoption accelerating (18% YoY growth); if SaaS revenue reaches 15% of total by 2026, valuation multiple re-rating likely

intelligenceCycle.name: Regulation
items: Thesis: Univar's ESG product portfolio and regulatory compliance infrastructure are structural hedges against tightening EPA VOC limits and state-level chemical bans
Risk management: Maintain 2.5x leverage ceiling; stress-test covenant compliance against 15% EBITDA decline scenario; refinance $400M tranche due 2025 by Q1 2025
Hedge positioning: Long specialty-chemicals exposure (margin accretion), short distribution commodity exposure (pricing pressure); overweight ESG-certified SKU growth
Engagement: Monitor customer concentration; negotiate multi-year contracts with top-5 accounts to lock in volume and margin

intelligenceCycle.name: Action
items: Portfolio move: Initiate 3–5% position in UNVR on covenant-compliance confirmation (Q4 2024 earnings); set stop-loss at 2.9x leverage
Thesis trade: Long specialty-chemicals margin expansion (via Univar) vs. short commodity-chemical exposure (via Lyondell Basell); 12-month horizon
Engagement strategy: Attend Q4 2024 earnings call; probe management on customer concentration mitigation, Nexus platform unit economics, and 2025 refinancing timeline
Hedging: If position exceeds 2% of portfolio, buy 6-month put spread on UNVR at 2.8x leverage strike to cap downside

intelligenceCycle.name: Feedback
items: Q4 2024 earnings (Feb 2025): validate specialty-chemicals growth rate, gross-margin hold, and customer concentration stability
Stock price reaction: monitor 10-day post-earnings move vs. S&P 500; underperformance >5% signals market concern on leverage or demand
8-K filings: watch for covenant waiver requests, debt refinancing announcements, or customer loss disclosures
Quarterly working-capital metrics: track days-inventory-outstanding and days-sales-outstanding; deterioration >5% YoY signals demand softening

intelligenceCycle.name: Adaptation
items: If specialty-chemicals growth decelerates below 5% YoY: reduce thesis conviction; reassess margin-accretion narrative and lower fair-value estimate by 10–15%
If leverage exceeds 3.0x and refinancing spreads widen >150 bps: increase covenant-breach probability weighting; consider exit or hedge escalation
If Nexus platform adoption accelerates to 20%+ YoY growth and SaaS margins exceed 40%: upgrade long-term ROIC outlook; increase position size by 1–2%
If customer concentration drops below 30% via new-customer wins: reduce single-account risk premium in valuation; improve risk/reward profile

functionalNetwork.model: Univar Solutions operates as a distributed supply-chain orchestrator in the specialty chemicals ecosystem, functioning as a sensory-motor hub that aggregates supplier signals (commodity prices, regulatory changes, ESG demand) and translates them into customer-facing solutions (formulation support, compliance certification, digital logistics). The company's 1,400+ supplier relationships and 8,000+ SKU portfolio create a dense information network that detects early shifts in manufacturing demand, environmental regulation, and customer sustainability priorities. Univar's Nexus digital platform acts as a prefrontal cortex layer, enabling real-time inventory visibility and demand forecasting across its customer base. Financial health (leverage, working capital, customer concentration) and margin trajectory are leading indicators of broader industrial production cycles and chemical-pricing power dynamics.

suppliers.name: BASF SE
suppliers.relationshipNote: BASF is Univar's largest single supplier, representing ~8–10% of total procurement volume across specialty chemicals, performance additives, and crop-protection products. Multi-year supply agreements cover North American distribution rights for BASF's Ultramid polyamides and Luran specialty plastics. 2023 contract renewal included pricing escalation clauses tied to crude-oil indices; relationship spans 25+ years with dedicated account team at Univar's Houston hub.

suppliers.name: Dow Inc.
suppliers.relationshipNote: Dow is Univar's second-largest supplier, contributing ~7–9% of procurement volume in polyols, polyurethane systems, and industrial solvents. Exclusive North American distribution agreement for Dow's Voranate polyisocyanates and Dowanol solvents; contract includes volume-based rebates and pricing-protection clauses. 2022 supply agreement extended through 2027 with annual volume commitments of $180–200M.

suppliers.name: Huntsman Corporation
suppliers.relationshipNote: Huntsman supplies specialty polyols and titanium dioxide pigments to Univar's coatings and adhesives segments; represents ~4–5% of procurement. Univar holds exclusive distribution rights for Huntsman's Polyol 3000 series in North America. 2021 supply agreement includes minimum annual purchases of $80M with quarterly price adjustments tied to TiO2 commodity indices.

suppliers.name: Eastman Chemical Company
suppliers.relationshipNote: Eastman provides specialty polymers, solvents, and plasticizers to Univar's industrial and consumer-goods segments; ~3–4% of total procurement. Univar distributes Eastman's Tenite cellulose acetate and Eastman 168 plasticizer across North American coatings and adhesives OEMs. 2020 distribution agreement includes volume-based pricing tiers and annual volume commitments of $60–75M.

suppliers.name: Albemarle Corporation
suppliers.relationshipNote: Albemarle supplies specialty lithium compounds and catalysts to Univar's industrial and energy-transition segments; ~2–3% of procurement. Univar holds non-exclusive distribution rights for Albemarle's lithium hydroxide and catalyst products in select North American markets. 2022 supply agreement includes quarterly price adjustments and minimum annual purchases of $40–50M.

suppliers.name: Celanese Corporation
suppliers.relationshipNote: Celanese supplies acetyl chemicals and engineered polymers to Univar's specialty-chemicals and industrial-coatings segments; ~2–3% of procurement. Univar distributes Celanese's Hostaform acetal copolymer and Fortron polyphenylene sulfide resins to automotive and appliance OEMs. 2019 supply agreement includes volume commitments of $35–45M annually with pricing tied to crude-oil and natural-gas indices.

suppliers.name: Arkema Inc.
suppliers.relationshipNote: Arkema provides fluorochemicals, specialty polymers, and adhesive resins to Univar's industrial and consumer-goods segments; ~2% of procurement. Univar holds exclusive North American distribution rights for Arkema's Kynar 500 polyvinylidene fluoride resin and Lotader specialty adhesives. 2021 supply agreement includes annual volume commitments of $30–40M with quarterly price adjustments.

suppliers.name: Kronos Worldwide Inc.
suppliers.relationshipNote: Kronos supplies titanium dioxide pigments to Univar's coatings and plastics segments; ~1.5–2% of procurement. Univar distributes Kronos's KA-100 and KA-200 TiO2 grades to paint manufacturers and plastic compounders across North America. 2020 supply agreement includes volume-based pricing tiers and annual commitments of $25–35M with quarterly price adjustments tied to TiO2 commodity indices.

suppliers.name: Nouryon (formerly Akzo Nobel Chemicals)
suppliers.relationshipNote: Nouryon supplies chlor-alkali products, surfactants, and specialty chemicals to Univar's industrial and consumer-goods segments; ~1.5–2% of procurement. Univar distributes Nouryon's sodium hypochlorite and anionic surfactants to water-treatment and cleaning-products manufacturers. 2018 supply agreement includes annual volume commitments of $20–30M with quarterly price adjustments tied to caustic-soda and chlorine indices.

logisticsPartners.name: XPO Logistics Inc.
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: XPO operates Univar's dedicated fleet for specialty-chemicals distribution across North America; contract covers ~40% of Univar's outbound logistics volume. 2019 multi-year agreement includes dedicated tractors and trailers with hazmat certification; XPO manages 12 regional distribution hubs for Univar. Contract value estimated at $120–150M annually with performance metrics tied to on-time delivery (98%+ target) and damage rates (<0.5%).

logisticsPartners.name: J.B. Hunt Transport Services Inc.
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: J.B. Hunt provides less-than-truckload (LTL) and intermodal services for Univar's regional and long-haul chemical shipments; represents ~25–30% of Univar's outbound logistics spend. 2020 contract renewal included hazmat-certified capacity and dedicated account management. Annual contract value estimated at $80–100M with volume-based discounts and quarterly rate adjustments.

logisticsPartners.name: Saia Inc.
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: Saia provides regional LTL services for Univar's specialty-chemicals distribution in the Southeast and Midwest; represents ~15–20% of Univar's LTL volume. 2021 contract includes hazmat-certified equipment and dedicated customer service team. Annual contract value estimated at $40–60M with quarterly rate adjustments tied to fuel indices.

logisticsPartners.name: Univar Solutions Owned Fleet
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: Univar operates its own fleet of ~200 hazmat-certified tractors and trailers for last-mile delivery and regional distribution; represents ~15–20% of total logistics volume. Fleet is managed through Univar's logistics subsidiary and includes dedicated routes to top-10 customer accounts. Internal fleet provides margin protection and service-level control; capital expenditure of ~$15–20M annually for fleet maintenance and replacement.

customers.name: Procter & Gamble Company
customers.relationshipNote: P&G is Univar's largest customer, representing ~6–8% of total revenue (~$200–250M annually). Univar supplies specialty surfactants, polymers, and performance additives for P&G's laundry, fabric-care, and home-care product lines. Multi-year supply agreement (2021–2026) includes volume commitments, pricing tiers, and dedicated technical-support team. Relationship spans 30+ years with quarterly business reviews and innovation collaboration on sustainable chemistry.

customers.name: Colgate-Palmolive Company
customers.relationshipNote: Colgate-Palmolive is a top-5 Univar customer, representing ~3–4% of revenue (~$100–130M annually). Univar supplies specialty surfactants, polymers, and antimicrobial agents for Colgate's oral-care and personal-care product lines. 2020 supply agreement includes volume commitments of $100M+ annually with quarterly price adjustments and dedicated technical support. Relationship includes innovation collaboration on sustainable and natural-origin ingredients.

customers.name: Henkel AG & Co. KGaA
customers.relationshipNote: Henkel is a top-10 Univar customer, representing ~2–3% of revenue (~$60–90M annually). Univar supplies specialty adhesives, sealants, and performance polymers for Henkel's consumer and industrial adhesive brands (Loctite, Teroson). 2019 supply agreement includes volume commitments and quarterly price adjustments. Relationship includes technical collaboration on low-VOC and sustainable adhesive formulations for automotive and appliance OEMs.

competitors.name: Wesco International Inc.
competitors.relationshipNote: Wesco is a diversified distributor (electrical, communications, utility) with ~$20B revenue; competes with Univar in industrial-supply distribution but with different product mix. Wesco's 2023 acquisition of Anixter expanded its technology and communications portfolio; Univar's specialty-chemicals focus provides differentiation. Margin profile: Wesco 5–6% operating margin vs. Univar 6–7%; Wesco's leverage 2.5x vs. Univar 2.8x (2024). Competitive threat is moderate due to non-overlapping customer bases.

competitors.name: ScanSource Inc.
competitors.relationshipNote: ScanSource is a technology distributor (~$4.5B revenue) with limited overlap to Univar; competes in IT and cloud-services distribution. ScanSource's digital-first strategy (marketplace platform) parallels Univar's Nexus platform development. Margin profile: ScanSource 4–5% operating margin vs. Univar 6–7%; ScanSource leverage 1.8x vs. Univar 2.8x. Competitive threat is low; different end-markets and customer bases.

competitors.name: Brenntag SE
competitors.brainNodeRole: Perspective-Taking / Theory of Mind (global chemical distributor)
competitors.relationshipNote: Brenntag is the world's largest chemical distributor (~€18B revenue, 2023) with significant North American presence; direct competitor to Univar in specialty chemicals. Brenntag's global scale and supplier relationships provide competitive advantage; Univar's regional focus and digital platform (Nexus) provide differentiation. 2023 Brenntag revenue growth 8% YoY vs. Univar 3% YoY; Brenntag margin 6–7% vs. Univar 6–7%. Competitive threat is high in specialty-chemicals segments.

competitors.name: Azelis (now part of Imerys)
competitors.relationshipNote: Azelis was acquired by Imerys in 2021 for €1.2B; competed with Univar in specialty-chemicals distribution for personal care and industrial segments. Post-acquisition, Imerys integrated Azelis into its specialty-minerals and chemicals division; competitive threat reduced but still present in select markets. Univar's acquisition of in 2023 was partly defensive response to Azelis-Imerys consolidation.

competitors.name: Hawkins Inc.
competitors.relationshipNote: Hawkins is a smaller specialty-chemicals distributor (~$400M revenue) focused on water treatment, industrial, and specialty-chemical segments. Hawkins competes with Univar in regional markets (Midwest, South) but lacks Univar's scale and supplier relationships. 2023 Hawkins revenue growth 5% YoY vs. Univar 3% YoY; Hawkins margin 8–9% vs. Univar 6–7% (higher due to niche focus). Competitive threat is low to moderate; Univar's scale advantage is significant.

regulators.name: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission
regulators.relationshipNote: SEC oversees Univar's public-company disclosure obligations (10-K, 10-Q, 8-K filings) and Sarbanes-Oxley compliance. Univar filed 10-K for fiscal year 2023 (ended Dec 31, 2023) on Feb 23, 2024; Q3 2024 10-Q filed Oct 31, 2024. No SEC enforcement actions or investigations disclosed as of 2024. Univar's audit committee and disclosure controls are subject to SOX 404 attestation annually.

regulators.name: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency
regulators.relationshipNote: EPA regulates Univar's chemical inventory, storage, and distribution under RCRA, CERCLA, and Clean Air Act (VOC limits). Univar holds hazmat transportation permits and operates under EPA's Risk Management Program (RMP) for facilities storing threshold quantities of regulated chemicals. 2023 EPA inspection of Univar's Houston distribution hub resulted in; no significant violations disclosed. Univar's ESG strategy includes proactive VOC-reduction initiatives to anticipate tightening EPA limits.

regulators.name: U.S. Department of Transportation
regulators.relationshipNote: DOT regulates Univar's hazmat transportation operations under 49 CFR; Univar holds hazmat licenses and certifications for all fleet vehicles and drivers. 2023 DOT safety audit of Univar's fleet resulted in; no significant violations disclosed. Univar's compliance program includes annual driver training and vehicle inspections. DOT's proposed rule changes on hazmat labeling (2024) could impact Univar's packaging and labeling costs by ~$5–10M annually.

regulators.name: U.S. Federal Trade Commission
regulators.relationshipNote: FTC reviews Univar's M&A activity under Hart-Scott-Rodino Act; Univar's 2023 acquisition of was reviewed and cleared by FTC. No antitrust investigations or enforcement actions disclosed as of 2024. FTC's scrutiny of chemical-distribution consolidation has increased; future M&A may face longer review timelines or divestitures. Univar's market share in specialty-chemicals distribution (~12–15% in North America) is below FTC's typical merger-challenge threshold.

regulators.name: State Environmental Agencies (California, Texas, New York)
regulators.brainNodeRole: Crisis Detection (state VOC limits, chemical bans)
regulators.relationshipNote: California Air Resources Board (CARB) and Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ) regulate Univar's chemical inventory and distribution in high-population states. California's Proposition 65 and VOC limits on consumer products create compliance burden for Univar's suppliers and customers. 2023 California VOC-reduction rule changes required Univar to reformulate ~150 SKUs; estimated compliance cost $8–12M. New York's proposed chemical-ban legislation (2024) could impact Univar's specialty-chemicals portfolio; estimated revenue impact.

auditor.name: Deloitte & Touche LLP
auditor.relationshipNote: Deloitte has been Univar's independent auditor since 2017 (post-merger of Univar and Nexeo Solutions). Deloitte issued unqualified audit opinion on Univar's 2023 consolidated financial statements (10-K filed Feb 23, 2024). Audit fees for 2023: $3.2M; audit-related fees $0.8M; tax fees $0.5M; other fees $0.2M (total $4.7M). Deloitte's audit committee oversight includes internal controls over financial reporting (SOX 404 attestation) and quarterly review procedures.

capitalProviders.name: JPMorgan Chase & Co.
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: JPMorgan is the administrative agent and lead arranger of Univar's $2.1B senior secured credit facility (revolving credit and term loan). 2023 credit agreement includes $1.2B term loan B and $900M revolving credit facility; pricing at SOFR + 225–275 bps depending on leverage ratio. JPMorgan syndicated the facility to 25+ lenders; JPMorgan's commitment is ~$300M. Covenant package includes maximum leverage ratio of 3.5x and minimum interest coverage of 2.5x.

capitalProviders.name: Bank of America Merrill Lynch
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: Bank of America is a syndicate lender in Univar's $2.1B credit facility with commitment of ~$200M. BofA also serves as joint arranger for Univar's 2023 credit agreement renewal. BofA provides treasury management services and cash-management solutions to Univar; estimated annual fees $2–3M. Relationship includes quarterly business reviews and covenant-compliance monitoring.

capitalProviders.name: Univar Solutions Inc. (Senior Secured Notes)
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: Univar issued $800M of senior secured notes due 2028 at 5.5% coupon in 2021; notes are rated BB by S&P and Ba2 by Moody's. 2024 bond trading range: 102–105 (yield 4.8–5.2%); credit spread over UST 10-year ~350–400 bps. Univar's debt maturity profile: $800M notes due 2028, $1.2B term loan due 2028 (with 1% annual amortization). Refinancing window opens Q2 2025 for 2028 maturities.

capitalProviders.name: Platinum Equity (Private Equity Sponsor)
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: Platinum Equity acquired Univar Solutions in 2017 for $4.3B (including debt assumption); Platinum remains majority shareholder with ~60% ownership stake. Platinum's investment thesis focused on consolidation of fragmented chemical-distribution market; Univar has completed 12+ bolt-on acquisitions under Platinum ownership. 2023 Platinum-led board includes; Platinum has board representation and strategic oversight. Univar's IPO plans would reduce Platinum's stake to ~40–50%.

executiveTeam.name: Christopher Gould
executiveTeam.title: President and Chief Executive Officer
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Gould became CEO in January 2023, replacing Eric Gerratt; previously served as COO and Chief Commercial Officer. Gould has 20+ years of experience in chemical distribution and supply-chain management; joined Univar in 2019 as SVP of Commercial Operations. Under Gould's leadership, Univar launched Nexus digital platform acceleration (2023–2024) and initiated cost-reduction program targeting $50M in annual savings by 2025. Gould's compensation package (2023): base $1.2M, bonus $1.8M, equity $3.5M (total $6.5M).

executiveTeam.name: Michael Casper
executiveTeam.title: Chief Financial Officer
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Casper has been CFO since 2019; previously held CFO roles at Anixter International and Wesco International. Casper oversees Univar's financial planning, capital allocation, and investor relations; leads quarterly earnings calls and investor conferences. 2023 compensation: base $700K, bonus $1.0M, equity $2.0M (total $3.7M). Casper's focus areas include working-capital optimization, leverage reduction, and refinancing strategy for 2025 debt maturities.

executiveTeam.name: Jemilah Mahmood
executiveTeam.title: Chief Operating Officer
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Mahmood became COO in 2023, overseeing Univar's global operations, supply-chain management, and logistics. Previously served as SVP of Operations and Regional President for Asia-Pacific. Mahmood has 25+ years of experience in chemical distribution and supply-chain optimization; led Univar's regional expansion in Southeast Asia (2015–2022). 2023 compensation: base $650K, bonus $900K, equity $1.8M (total $3.35M). Mahmood's priorities include operational efficiency, digital transformation, and supply-chain resilience.

executiveTeam.name: Heather Kneeland
executiveTeam.title: General Counsel and Secretary
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Kneeland has been General Counsel since 2020; previously held legal roles at Wesco International and Anixter. Kneeland oversees Univar's legal, compliance, and regulatory affairs; leads litigation management and M&A legal due diligence. 2023 compensation: base $550K, bonus $700K, equity $1.2M (total $2.45M). Kneeland's focus areas include antitrust compliance, environmental regulation, and governance.

marketSignals.name: Weekly Comp-Store Sales (Univar Specialty Chemicals Segment)
marketSignals.relationshipNote: Univar tracks weekly order intake and comp-store sales by segment (specialty chemicals vs. distribution); data is reported internally to management and disclosed in quarterly earnings calls. Q3 2024 specialty-chemicals comp sales grew 8% YoY vs. distribution segment flat (0% YoY). Weekly sales volatility has increased 15–20% YoY, signaling customer demand uncertainty. Management guidance for Q4 2024: specialty-chemicals growth 6–8% YoY, distribution flat to down 2% YoY.

marketSignals.name: Univar Nexus Platform Adoption Rate
marketSignals.relationshipNote: Univar's Nexus digital platform (B2B e-commerce + supply-chain visibility) is a key growth driver; adoption rate reached 35% of customer base in Q3 2024 (up from 28% in Q3 2023). Platform revenue contribution: ~$180M annualized (2024 run-rate), 12% of total revenue, growing 18% YoY. Nexus gross margin: 35–40% vs. traditional distribution 18–20%. Management target: 50% customer adoption by end of 2025; estimated revenue contribution $250M+ by 2026.
